checks.description: the file is a ZIP that reads
receipt.json is present
receipt.json is valid JSON
spec_version is understood
receipt.json is in canonical form
required fields are present and typed
the signed subtree digests deterministically
the capture named by the receipt exists
the capture is the declared length
the capture hashes to the declared digest
the capture is a container this verifier reads
the capture is a readable WACZ
every WACZ resource matches its hash
the capture holds the document the claim describes
the claim carries a signature
the signature algorithm is supported
key_id is the digest of public_key
the signature verifies
the claim carries a time anchor
the time anchor verifies
the text fingerprint matches its definition

vectors.description: a signed receipt for one page, with no anchor
vectors.proves: the happy path verifies integrity and attribution, and reports time and currency as unchecked rather than as passes

vectors.description: the same receipt, checked against a key list that contains the signer
vectors.proves: key trust is reported separately: L1 says the signature is valid, and only a caller-supplied key list can say the key is one you meant to trust

vectors.description: a receipt whose claim carries no signature
vectors.proves: an unsigned receipt is not reported as a failure and not reported as verified: attribution is not_applicable, and the exit code distinguishes it from a broken receipt

vectors.description: a receipt checked against a key directory that vouches for the signing key
vectors.proves: section 6.7: trust arrives from the caller or not at all - a directory is the richer way of saying "this key is somebody's", and unlike a bare list of key ids it can also say whose, and until when

keys.name: Fixture Signer
keys.note: the key every signed fixture uses

vectors.description: a valid signature from a key the caller does not list
vectors.proves: an untrusted key does not make a receipt invalid, and does not make it trusted either

vectors.description: a capture of a page served over plain HTTP
vectors.proves: an insecure page is still worth recording, so it verifies and is caveated rather than failed

vectors.description: a receipt that declares a text fingerprint the capture actually has
vectors.proves: a fingerprint is checked rather than caveated: the words are re-extracted from the capture and hashed, so this level can pass - and a producer whose extractor disagreed with the definition is caught

vectors.description: a document that exercises every rule of section 4.5.1 at once
vectors.proves: the extraction is complete enough to reproduce a fingerprint from the rules alone: block and inline, the elements that are not read, the attributes that ask not to be read, named and numeric references, an unknown named one, an out-of-range numeric one, and the malformed markup a crawler fetched rather than a browser serialised

vectors.description: a document built to exercise the corners of section 4.5.1 that the other text fixture cannot reach
vectors.proves: the rules survive the shapes a real page arrives in: a hidden element with hidden children (so a skip has to count depth), a > inside a quoted attribute, a comment full of markup, an ampersand with no reference after it, an unknown name, a textarea whose content is text rather than markup, and an unterminated tag - which rule 7 says ends the document

vectors.description: a receipt whose text fingerprint is not the words in its own capture
vectors.proves: the fingerprint is checked against the capture, so a claim that says the page said something it did not is a failure - this is the shape of the bug this project's own fixture had, found by the check the fixture made necessary

vectors.description: a receipt carrying an extra field the spec does not define
vectors.proves: an unknown top-level field is inside the signed subtree: it cannot be added, removed or edited without the signature failing

vectors.description: the capture swapped for a different one of exactly the same length
vectors.proves: the digest check does work nothing else does: the length matches, the replacement capture is internally consistent, and only capture.digest notices

vectors.description: a WACZ whose record does not match the hash its own datapackage advertises
vectors.proves: the inner resource hashes catch content the outer container digest cannot see, and the receipts binds them because it was signed over exactly these bytes

vectors.description: the cited URL changed after the receipt was signed
vectors.proves: the signature covers the claim, not the file: editing a signed field leaves bytes that are canonical and a signature that means nothing. L0 also stops passing, because a claim naming a URL its capture holds no record for is a claim about a document this verifier cannot find - and it says so rather than assuming the document is fine

vectors.description: a receipt serialised with JSON.stringify instead of canonical form
vectors.proves: the signature still verifies and the receipt is still rejected, because the bytes that were signed are not the bytes that were delivered

vectors.description: a claim with a fractional byte count
vectors.proves: canonical-json-v1 admits integers only, so a float is a named failure rather than a rounding difference between two implementations

vectors.description: a file that is not a receipt at all
vectors.proves: an unreadable container fails at L0 and every later level says so, instead of reporting nothing and looking clean

vectors.description: a container that holds the claim but not the capture
vectors.proves: a claim without its bytes verifies nothing: the capture checks are not_checked with a reason, never silently absent

vectors.description: a claim that points its capture entry outside the container
vectors.proves: an entry name is untrusted input to a filesystem call, so it is refused at the shape check and never resolved

vectors.description: a receipt from a future version of the specification
vectors.proves: a version this verifier does not implement is a failure rather than a soft "unknown": nobody can honestly verify a claim they cannot read

vectors.description: a signature lifted from a different receipt
vectors.proves: the carried key is well formed, its id matches, the signature is a real Ed25519 signature - and it still fails, because it was made over another claim

vectors.description: a signature object with no key in it
vectors.proves: a malformed signature is a failure, not a gap - reporting "not checked" for something that is present and wrong would understate it

vectors.description: the first receipt in a chain
vectors.proves: a chain head has no link to follow, and saying so is a pass rather than a gap

vectors.description: a receipt that links to the previous one in its archive
vectors.proves: the link is only followed when the neighbour is supplied, and then it is actually compared

vectors.description: a receipt whose chain link does not match the neighbour supplied
vectors.proves: a broken chain link is a failure: the claim is intact and the archive it claims to belong to is not

vectors.description: a chain receipt verified without its neighbour
vectors.proves: an unfollowed link is not_checked, not a pass: the receipt stays verified on integrity and attribution, and the summary says why the ordering is unproven

vectors.description: a chain head that names a predecessor
vectors.proves: a receipt cannot be both the start of a chain and a link in one

vectors.description: a claim that declares a text fingerprint and a capture whose page cannot be found
vectors.proves: a fingerprint is only checkable against a document, so when there is no document the check is not_checked - never a failure, because the claim may be perfectly honest and the capture simply not one this reader can open

vectors.description: a claim whose text fingerprint names a normalization this verifier does not implement
vectors.proves: a normalization is named by the claim, so a verifier that does not implement it says so rather than checking the digest against the wrong procedure - and an unimplemented normalization does not un-verify the bytes, because it is a gap in the verifier and not a fault in the receipt

vectors.description: a claim with no spec_version at all
vectors.proves: the two checks that could answer this are different sentences - a version this verifier does not read, and a claim that is not shaped like a claim - and the specification should say which one a missing version is, because two implementations guessing differently would report different levels for the same receipt

vectors.description: a capture whose datapackage advertises no WARC record at all
vectors.proves: the record layer refuses by name: a capture that advertises nothing to read is not_checked on the document - a gap in the reader and not a fault in the receipt - while its own resource hashes, which are the part it does describe, are still checked and still pass

vectors.description: a capture whose WARC holds a different page from the one the claim cites
vectors.proves: the reader matches WARC-Target-URI exactly rather than falling back to whatever record it finds first: "no record for your page" is a fact the caller needs, and picking another page would report a document the claim never described

vectors.description: a capture that states a WARC-Payload-Digest its own payload does not have
vectors.proves: a capture that disagrees with itself about its own bytes is not one to read a document out of, so the reader refuses by name rather than hashing what it found - and the record is a plain uncompressed WARC, which is the other half of what this vector covers

vectors.description: a claim whose capture entry name carries a colon
vectors.proves: section 12: a colon is a drive letter or an NTFS alternate data stream on Windows and has no business in a receipt, so the name is refused at the shape check even though it resolves nowhere near the filesystem on the machine checking it

vectors.description: a claim that has been canonically rewritten without its tool block
vectors.proves: manifest.shape is about the claim being a claim at all: a required field that is absent stops the capture stage before anything is looked up with the claim's names, and the signature is still checked - a malformed receipt and a forged one are different sentences

vectors.description: a token signed by a pinned certificate that is not a timestamping one
vectors.proves: section 8.3 step 1, second half: a pin is not a licence to skip the protocol - RFC 3161 requires the timeStamping extended key usage, so a pinned certificate without it is a failure rather than an untested pass

vectors.description: a token whose genTime falls outside the signing certificate's validity window
vectors.proves: section 8.3 step 3: a timestamp is only as good as the certificate that made it, so a stamp from outside that window is a failure - and because this format consults no revocation list, a certificate valid at the time may still have been revoked, which the verdict does not pretend otherwise about

vectors.description: a receipt carrying an RFC 3161 timestamp token, checked with no TSA pinned
vectors.proves: a token is not validated against a list this project invented: with nothing pinned it is unsupported and caveated, and never counts as time established

vectors.description: a timestamp token that commits to this claim, signed by a TSA the caller pinned
vectors.proves: the whole of section 8.3: the imprint is the claim hash, the certificate was valid when it stamped, it is a timestamping certificate, and the signature verifies - so L2 passes and the attested instant is reported as a bound

vectors.description: a timestamp token whose imprint is not this claim
vectors.proves: a token that answers a different digest is a failure with both digests named, even though the signature over it is genuine: being signed by a TSA is not the same as being about this claim

vectors.description: a timestamp token signed by a TSA the caller did not pin
vectors.proves: an anchor from an authority the caller does not trust is not checked and not blamed: the receipt stays verified, L2 says not_checked, and the token's own fingerprint is named so the caller can pin it if they choose

vectors.description: a receipt with an anchor type that does not exist
vectors.proves: an unknown anchor is unsupported rather than a failure: this verifier does not know whether it is broken, and says so

vectors.description: a receipt with an extra file that no rule covers
vectors.proves: content outside the claim and the capture is reported as a caveat rather than ignored, because nothing signs it

vectors.description: a container with a capture but no claim
vectors.proves: a container without a claim is not a receipt: the missing file is a failure and every later check says it never ran

vectors.description: a receipt.json that is not JSON
vectors.proves: unparseable bytes are a failure at the container level, not an empty verdict

vectors.description: a claim that understates the size of its own capture
vectors.proves: the declared length is checked separately from the digest, so a claim that is wrong about its bytes says so precisely

vectors.description: a claim whose capture is a container this verifier does not read
vectors.proves: an unreadable kind of capture is unsupported rather than failed, and the receipt is still not verified

vectors.description: a capture that is not a container at all, correctly hashed
vectors.proves: the digest being right is not the same as the capture being readable, and the two failures are reported separately

vectors.description: a receipt whose key id does not match the key it carries
vectors.proves: key ids are derived, not asserted: a mismatch is caught before the signature itself is even examined

vectors.description: a receipt signed with an algorithm this verifier does not implement
vectors.proves: an unimplemented algorithm leaves the receipt unverified with no failure recorded, which is why the exit codes have three values and not two

vectors.description: a chain anchor added to a receipt after it was signed
vectors.proves: the obvious implementation of "exclude the anchor from the signature" would let anyone add one and manufacture an L2 pass; signing every anchor that could have existed at signing time makes it break the signature instead

vectors.description: a capture that says what kind of capture it is
vectors.proves: the profile is reported rather than judged: verification is unchanged, and a reader is told which kind of capture they are holding

vectors.description: a capture whose declared kind this verifier does not interpret
vectors.proves: an unknown profile is neither a pass nor a failure: the bytes are checked, the meaning is caveated, and the receipt stays verified on integrity and attribution

vectors.description: a claim whose document digest describes a different document
vectors.proves: the claim is checked against the capture rather than taken at its word: a producer that hashed something other than what it wrote is caught, which is the "lying author" the threat model has named since its first draft

vectors.description: a claim whose document digest is right and whose length is not
vectors.proves: the length is checked as well as the digest, because it is the one a person checks by eye and "another size" is a different sentence from "different bytes"

vectors.description: a claim with a C0 control character in an undocumented field
vectors.proves: the escaping rule from the outside: `\b \t \n \f \r` use short forms, every other C0 control is a lowercase \u escape, and DEL, non-ASCII and astral characters are emitted as themselves. The rule was unexercised by any vector until a second implementation was written against it

vectors.description: a claim whose delivered bytes contain `-0`
vectors.proves: `-0` has no canonical spelling, and this is the one rule that cannot be enforced after parsing in every language: JavaScript keeps the sign through JSON.parse and refuses it, Python loses it and has to read the raw bytes. The vector pins the behaviour either way

vectors.description: a capture that declares itself the bytes a server sent
vectors.proves: a *recognised* profile is reported without a caveat, so the caveat above means "unknown" rather than "declared"
